ד' מִצְוֹת יֵשׁ בְּפוּרִים, מִקְרָא מְגִלָּה וּמִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת וּמַתָּנוֹת
 לָאֶבְיוֹנִים וּמִשְׁתֶּה וְשִׂמְחָה. ונ"ל שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד ד' אוֹתִיּוֹת שֵׁם הוֹי' ב"ה, דְּמִלְחָמָה לְשֵׁם זֶה בַּעֲמָלֵק מִדּוֹר דּוֹר', וְהַנִּצּוּחַ הוּא ע"י ד' מִצְוֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת אֵלּוּ.
There are four mitzvot on Purim: reading the Megillah, sending portions of food, gifts to the poor, and feasting and joy. It seems to me that they correspond to the four letters of the name of God, blessed be He, for the war against this name is with Amalek from generation to generation, and victory is through these four practical mitzvot.
1. בשלח יז, טז: כי יד על כס יה מלחמה להוי"ה בעמלק מדור דור.
 * Exodus 17:16: "Because a hand is on the throne of God; the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation."
דְּכָל מִצְוֹת שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לְזֵכֶר הַנֵּס הוּא מָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם כֹּחַ וְחִיּוּת שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָיָה הַיְּשׁוּעָה בְּפֹעַל, וע"י אוֹתָם מִצְוֹת מִתַּגְלִית אוֹתָהּ יְשׁוּעָה בְּפֹעַל בְּכָל דּוֹר. וְעִקָּר
For all the mitzvot that are done in memory of the miracle are things that have in them the power and vitality that was revealed at the time of the event in which the salvation occurred in actuality. And through those mitzvot, that same salvation is revealed in actuality in every generation. 
הַיְּשׁוּעָה הוּא כְּשֶׁנּוֹשָׁעִים בְּאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם חִסָּרוֹן שֶׁמֵּחֲמָתוֹ בָּאָה הַצָּרָה, דֶזֶּהוּ כָּל יְשׁוּעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל יְשׁוּעַת הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְלֹא יְשׁוּעַת הַגּוּפוֹת בִּלְבַד. וְכָל הַצָּרָה בָּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה שֶׁמִּזֶּה יִצְמַח הַיְּשׁוּעָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וּמִמַּכּוֹתֶיךָ אֶרְפָּאֲךָ
 The core
of salvation is when one is saved through that very thing in which they were lacking, on account of which the trouble came, for this is the entirety of Israel's salvation, salvation of the soul and not just salvation of the body. And every trouble comes because of that from which salvation will sprout, and as it is said, "And from your wounds I will heal you."
2. ירמיה ל, יז: כי אעלה ארוכה לך וממכותיך ארפאך נאם ה'
 * Jeremiah 30:17: "For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds, says the Lord."
ר"ל מֵהַמַּכּוֹת עַצְמָם וְעַל יָדָם הוּא הָרְפוּאָה; וְכֵן מִשָּׁם יִקְבְּצֵךְ וּמִשָּׁם יִקָּחֵךְ
Meaning, from the wounds themselves and through them is the healing; and similarly, "From there He will gather you, and from there He will take you."
3. נצבים ל, ד: אם יהיה נדחך בקצה השמים משם יקבצך ה' אלהיך ומשם יקחך.
 * Deuteronomy 30:4: "Even if your outcasts are at the ends of the heavens, from there the Lord your God will gather you, and from there He will take you."
הַיְנוּ מִשָּׁם דַּיְּקָא יִצְמַח הַקִּבּוּץ וְשֶׁיִּקָּחֵךְ. וכמ"ש בַּמְּגִלָּה (י"ד ע"א) גְּדוֹלָה הֲסָרַת טַבַּעַת כו' שֶׁהֶחֱזִירָתַן לְמוּטָב
That is, precisely from there will the gathering and taking sprout. And as it says in the Megillah (14a), "Greater was the removal of the ring, etc., that it returned them to good."
4. ויסר המלך את טבעתו. אמר רבי אבא בר כהנא, גדולה הסרת טבעת יותר מארבעים ושמונה נביאים ושבע נביאות שנתנבאו להן לישראל, שכולן לא החזירום למוטב ואילו הסרת הטבעת החזירתן למוטב (שגזרו עליהן תעניות לתשובה, כדכתיב צום ובכי ומספד שק ואפר יוצע לרבים. רש"י).
 * "And the king removed his ring." Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: The removal of the ring was greater than the forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses who prophesied to Israel, for all of them did not return them [Israel] to good, whereas the removal of the ring did return them to good (for they decreed fasts upon themselves for repentance, as it is written "fasting, weeping and lamenting; sackcloth and ashes were spread out for many." Rashi).
וְלָקְחוּ לְמָשָׁל זֶה בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (צ"ז ע"ב) מַעֲמִיד לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ קָשֶׁה כְּהָמָן
And they took as a parable for this in chapter Chelek (97b), "He raises up for them a king as harsh as Haman."
5. רבי אליעזר אומר, אם ישראל עושין תשובה נגאלין ואם לאו אין נגאלין. א"ל רבי יהושע, אם אין עושין תשובה אין נגאלין, אלא הקב"ה מעמיד להן מלך שגזרותיו קשות כהמן וישראל עושין תשובה ומחזירן למוטב. 
 * Rabbi Eliezer says: If Israel repents, they will be redeemed, and if not, they will not be redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: If they do not repent, they are not redeemed? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, raises up for them a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, and Israel repents and He returns them to good.
דְּבִימֵי הָמָן שָׁבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵמָה וְקִבְּלוּ עַל עַצְמָם וְעַל זַרְעָם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה. וְזֶהוּ עִקַּר הַיְּשׁוּעָה שֶׁהָיְתָה ע"י גְּזֵרָה זוֹ, שֶׁזָּכוּ לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה וְשָׁבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵמָה, וּמִמֵּילָא נִתְבַּטְּלָה הַגְּזֵרָה, כִּי אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר לְאַבְּדָם ח"ו עוֹד דַּאֲפִלּוּ צִיפְּרָא מִבַּלְעֲדֵי שְׁמַיָּא כו
For in the days of Haman, they returned in complete repentance and accepted upon themselves and upon their descendants the entire Torah out of love. And this is the essence of the salvation that was through this decree, that they merited to accept the words of Torah out of love and they returned in complete repentance, and automatically the decree was annulled, for how is it possible to destroy them, God forbid, any longer, since even a bird without Heaven, etc.?
6. בראשית רבה פע"ט, ו: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי ורבי אלעזר בריה הוו טמירין במערתא כו' (היו נחבאים שמה מפני המלכות. מ"כ), לסוף שלש עשרה שנין נפק יתיב על תרע מערתא (יצא לו ר"ש על פתח המערה), חמא חד צייד קאים וצייד ציפורין (ראה צייד אחד שעמד וצד עופות), וכד הוה שמע רבי שמעון ברת קלא אמרה מן שמיא דימוס (כשהיה ר"ש שומע בת קול אומרת מן השמים דימוס, ל' רחמים והצלה) הות פסגא (היה אותו עוף ניצל ובורח), וכד הוה שמע ברת קלא אמרת ספקולא (ל' מיתה ועונש) הות מתצדה ונלכדה (היה אותו עוף ניצוד ונלכד בפח הצייד). אמר, ציפור מבלעדי שמיא לא מתצדא, על אחת כמה וכמה נפש בר נש (צפור אינו ניצוד בלעדי גזירה מן השמים, על אחת כמה וכמה נפש בן אדם; לפיכך אלך לי אל מקומי, ואם אינו נגזר מן השמים לא אמות).
 * Genesis Rabbah 79:6: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai and Rabbi Elazar his son were hiding in a cave, etc. (they were hiding there from the government. M.K.). After thirteen years, he went out and sat at the entrance of the cave (R. Shimon went out to the entrance of the cave). He saw a hunter standing and hunting birds (he saw a hunter who was standing and hunting birds). And when Rabbi Shimon heard a Bat Kol (heavenly voice) saying from Heaven "Dimos" (a word of mercy and salvation), it would escape (that bird would be saved and escape). And when he heard the Bat Kol say "Spekula" (a word of death and punishment) it would be caught and trapped (that bird would be caught and trapped in the hunter's snare). He said: "A bird is not caught without Heaven, all the more so the soul of a man" (A bird is not caught without a decree from Heaven, all the more so the soul of a man; therefore, I will go to my place, and if it is not decreed from Heaven, I will not die).
וְהַגְּזֵרָה הָיְתָה מֶה' בַּמִּשְׁפָּט תְּחִלָּה.
And the decree was from God, in judgment, at the beginning.
ואע"פ שֶׁכְּבָר הִבְטִיחַ הַשַּׁ"י וְאַף גַּם זֹאת בִּהְיוֹתָם וְגֵו' לֹא וְגֵו' לְכַלּוֹתָם וגו"י 
And even though God had already promised, "Yet for all that, when they are, etc., I will not, etc., to destroy them, etc."
7. בחוקותי כו, מד: ואף גם זאת בהיותם בארץ אויביהם לא מאסתים ולא געלתים לכלותם להפר בריתי אתם כי אני ה' אלהיהם (ובמגילה יא, א: שמואל אמר, לא מאסתים ולא געלתים לכלותם לא מאסתים בימי יוונים, ולא געלתים בימי אספסיינוס, לכלותם בימי המן). 
 * Leviticus 26:44: "Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not cast them away, nor will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly and to break My covenant with them; for I am the Lord their God" (And in Megillah 11a: Shmuel said, "I will not cast them away, nor will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly" – "I did not cast them away" in the days of the Greeks, "nor will I abhor them" in the days of Vespasian, "to destroy them utterly" in the days of Haman).
 וְכֵן בְּכַמָּה מִקְרָאוֹת, אֲבָל כְּבָר אָמְרוּ זַ"ל (מְגִלָּה י"ג ע"ב) לֵיכָּא דְּיָדַע לִשָּׁנָא בִּישָׁא כְּהָמָן. 
And similarly in many verses. But the Sages of blessed memory already said (Megillah 13b), "There is none who knows evil speech like Haman."
 8. ישנו עם אחד. אמר רבא, ליכא דידע לישנא בישא כהמן. אמר ליה תא ניכלינהו, אמר ליה מסתפינא מאלהיו דלא ליעביד בי כדעבד בקמאי, אמר ליה ישנו מן המצות. אמר ליה אית בהו רבנן, אמר ליה עם אחד הן.
 * "There is a certain people." Rava said: There is none who knows evil speech like Haman. He [Ahasuerus] said to him [Haman], "Come, let us consume them." He [Haman] said to him, "I am afraid of their God, lest He do to me as He did to the previous ones." He [Ahasuerus] said to him, "They have become lax from the commandments." He [Haman] said to him, "There are Rabbis among them." He [Ahasuerus] said to him, "They are one people."
וְאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה פ"ג) דְּכָל מֶלֶךְ סְתָם בממ"ה הקב"ה מְדַבֵּר
And they said in the Midrash (Esther Rabbah 3) that every unspecified "king" [in the Megillah] refers to the Holy One, blessed be He.
9. פיסקא י: רבי יודן ורבי לוי בשם רבי יוחנן, כל מקום שנאמר במגלה זו למלך אחשורוש - במלך אחשורוש הכתוב מדבר, וכל מקום שנאמר למלך סתם - משמש קדש וחול.
 * Passage 10: Rabbi Yudan and Rabbi Levi in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Every place where it says in this Megillah "King Ahasuerus" - the verse is speaking about King Ahasuerus. And every place where it says "the king" without specification - it serves both sacred and mundane.
text.5_Chapter, 1_Paragraph:
א"כ כָּל דְּבָרָיו וּלְמֶלֶךְ אֵין שָׁוֶה וְגֵו' אֶשְׁקֹל אֶל גִּנְזֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ10 הוּא כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה. 
Therefore, all of his words, "and it is not befitting the king, etc." "I will weigh into the king's treasuries" are directed upwards.
10. אסתר ג, ח-ט: ישנו עם אחד מפוזר ומפורד בין העמים בכל מדינות מלכותך ודתיהם שונות מכל עם ואת דתי המלך אינם עושים ולמלך אין שוה להניחם. אם על המלך טוב יכתב לאבדם, ועשרת אלפים ככר כסף אשקול על ידי עושי המלאכה להביא אל גנזי המלך. 
 * Esther 3:8-9: "There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom; and their laws are different from those of every other people, and they do not keep the king's laws. Therefore, it is not befitting the king to tolerate them. If it please the king, let it be written that they be destroyed; and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who have charge of the king's business, to bring it into the king's treasuries."
 וְתֶחֱלֶה קִטְרֵג עֲלֵיהֶם מֵחֲטָאֵיהֶם, כִּי כְּבָר קִלְקְלוּ לְגַמְרֵי כָּל קוֹמַת הָאָדָם; שֶׁחָלוּק לֵד' שֶׁהֵם ה', כַּנּוֹדָע חֲלֻקַּת נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם לָה' מַדְרִיגוֹת נרנח"י, וְהֵם נֶגֶד ד' עוֹלָמוֹת אבי"ע, וּבְסוֹד ד' אוֹתִיּוֹת הַשֵּׁם וְקוֹצוֹ שֶׁל י'.
And he began to prosecute them based on their sins, for they had already completely corrupted the entire stature of man; which is divided into five, which are the five, as is known, the division of the human soul into five levels: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah and they correspond to the four worlds, Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, and in the secret of the four letters of the Name and the tip of the 'Yud'.
וְאָמַר יָשְׁנוּ עַם אֶחָד שֶׁיְּשֵׁנִים מִן הַמַּצּוֹת, זֶהוּ נְפִילַת הַמֹּחִין דֻּבַּעַתְּ הַשֵּׁנָה. שאע"פ שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁבַּמֹּחַ טְהוֹרָה. 
And he said "a certain people" who are sleeping from the commandments. This is the falling of the mochin (intellect) because of sleep. Even though the soul in the brain is pure.
11. ברכת אלקי נשמה: נשמה שנתת בי טהורה היא.
 * The blessing of "Elokai Neshamah": "The soul that You have given me is pure."
וְהֵם חֶלְקֵי חַיָּה יְחִידָה, דְּבֶהָם אֵין מְצִיאוּת שׁוּם פְּגָם, מ"מ טָעַן דְּכֶבָּר נִסְתַּלְּקוּ מֵהֶם לְגַמְרֵי וְאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּכוּת עוֹד עִמָּהֶם. וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר עַם אֶחָד, לְרַמֵּז עַל חֵלֶק יְחִידָה הָרָמוּז בְּקוֹצוֹ שֶׁל י', דַּשָּׁם אֵין שׁוּם חִלּוּק וּפֵרוּד כְּלָל בֵּין כְּלַל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל; וְגַם שָׁם הוּא הַשֵּׁנָה וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת אוֹתוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ.
And those are parts of Chayah and Yechidah, in which there is no possibility of any flaw. Nevertheless, he argued that they had already been completely removed from them and they no longer had any connection with them. And this is what he said, "a certain people", to allude to the part of Yechidah that is hinted at in the tip of the 'Yud', for there is no division or separation at all between all the souls of Israel; and even there is the sleep and removal of that root.
וּמְפֻזָּר וּמְפֹרָד הָיִינוּ שֶׁאֵינָם בְּאַחְדוּת וְיֵשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶם פֵּרוּד לְבָבוֹת. וְדָבָר זֶה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין הַלֵּב בִּשְׁלֵמוּת לִהְיוֹת דָּבוּק בהש"י כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לְלָבָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּאָז הָיוּ כָּל הַלְּבָבוֹת מְיֻחָדוֹת יַחַד וְלֹא הָיָה פֵּרוּד כְּלָל. וּמִצַּד זֶה מַגִּיעַ הַפְּגָם לַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁהוּא מִכּוּרְסַיְן דְּעוֹלֵם הַבְּרִיאָה. 
And "scattered and dispersed" means that they are not in unity and there is separation of hearts between them. And this thing is because the heart is not complete in cleaving to God as is fitting for the hearts of Israel, for then all the hearts would be united together and there would be no separation at all. A Baraita is brought: The "Purim collection"—funds collected on Purim to distribute among the poor specifically for the Purim feast—must indeed be given to the poor for the Purim meal and not for any other purpose. Rabbi Elazar (Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua, a Tanna of the fourth generation) stated: provided that the poor person does not divert even a shoelace from this money to buy for his shoe—meaning the poor person is not permitted to use the money received for other needs, such as purchasing a shoelace for his shoe. Rather, he must spend all of the money exclusively on the Purim feast, as the funds were given to him explicitly for this purpose. (In "Tosefta Kepeshuta," it is written that Rabbi Elazar's prohibition applies specifically to non-food items; however, if the poor person has leftover money, he may spend it on other food-related needs, even if they are not directly connected to the Purim feast, since the money was provided for meal purposes.)
We do not strictly scrutinize ("medakdekin") the fulfillment of the mitzvah of Purim—meaning the charity given on Purim—to determine whether the recipient is genuinely poor and deserving or not. ("Mitzvah" here refers specifically to charity, as noted in "Devarim Rabbah," p. 36, note 10. According to the Yerushalmi as quoted by the early commentators, this phrase is understood as "Purim money.") Rather, anyone who extends his hand to receive money is given it, because this giving is not solely based on the laws of charity but also derives from the obligation of joy, as even wealthy people receive gifts of food ("mishloach manot").
We do not alter ("meshannin") Purim money—funds that one intended to distribute to the poor on Purim may not be redirected for another purpose (even another charitable cause). Rather, one must distribute this money to the poor specifically on Purim.
A question arises (as a suggested inference): Does this imply that regarding all other charity money, the law would be different, meaning one would indeed be permitted to redirect it for another purpose?! (This is asked rhetorically, with astonishment.) Clearly, one is not permitted to redirect charity money to other purposes!
The earlier statement is reconsidered and clarified accordingly: Rather, regarding all other charity money, if a person pledged to donate charity, as long as the money has not yet been handed over to the treasurers ("gizbarin," officials responsible for managing communal funds; the term originates from Persian), you—the donor—are permitted to redirect it for another charitable purpose. However, once the money has been given to the treasurers, you are no longer permitted to redirect it for another purpose without their consent. In contrast, Purim money may not be redirected for another purpose at all, even before it is transferred to the treasurers.
